texts.preamble: Sushil Kumar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 8 February, 2024 Author: Samit Gopal Bench: Samit Gopal High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad ?Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:22729 Court No. - 74 Case :- Criminal Revision No. - 599 of 2009 Revisionist :- Sushil Kumar Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another Counsel for Revisionist :- Rajiv Lochan Shukla Counsel for Opposite Party :- Govt. Advocate Hon'ble Samit Gopal,J. 1. List revised.
texts.facts: 5. The facts of the case are that N.R. Pandey, the Food Inspector found the revisionist on 30.11.2002 at about 12.00 p.m. at Nahar Bazar, Dibiyapur, District Auraiya, while he was selling pede (sweet made of khoya) without license. The food Inspector introduced himself and purchased 600 gm of pede from the revisionist by giving Rs. 42/- for sample and then kept in three plastic in equal quantity and after labelling it affixed seal on it which was then sent to the public analyst for chemical analysis and the chemical analyst after analysis found the sample to be adulterated in which starch was found. The complainant then took sanction from the C.M.O. concerned and filed a complaint against the revisionist/accused. In the trial court the complainant N.R. Pandey, the Food Inspector was examined as P.W.-1, Kush Kumar Gupta, Food Clerk was examined as PW-2. The accused/revisionist in his statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C. denied the prosecution case and stated of false implication.
texts.arguments: 6. Learned counsel for the revisionist argued that N.R. Pandey, the Food Inspector was examined as P.W.-1 under Section 244 Cr.P.C. and states of taking sample of pede from the revisionist. It is further argued that the notice under Section 13(2) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 has not been received by the revisionist. It is argued that there is nothing on record to show that the same as has been sent by the Food Inspector has been received by the revisionist and as such valuable right of the accused/revisionist safeguarding his interest is violated. To buttress the arguments learned counsel has placed the judgement of the Apex Court in the case of Vijendra vs. State of Uttar Pradesh: (2020) 15 SCC 763 (para-14 and 15) and Narayan Prasad Sahu vs. The State of Madhya Pradesh: (2022) 1 SCC 87 (para-5, 6, 8 and 9). It is argued that in the trial P.W.-2 Kush Kumar Gupta, the Food Clerk although states of sending notice u/s 13 (2) of the Act through the registered post but also states that he has no information regarding the receipt of the same by the accused. It is argued that the trial court while dealing with the said issue although has stated that the said witness has not referred to and stated regarding the fact of receipt of the said notice by the accused but the accused has not produced any evidence from his side which would go to show that he has not received any notice u/s 13 (2) of the Act. The said finding is incomplete and would not stand to the test of the view as held by the Apex Court in the above two judgement in as much as the trial court is expected to return a specific finding regarding the receipt of the notice by the accused. Since there is no such affirmative finding by the trial court regarding receipt of the notice notice u/s 13 (2) of the Act by the accused-revisionist it cannot be said that the said notice was received by him. It is argued that the present revision thus deserved to be allowed. 7. Learned counsel for the State opposed the prayer and arguments and argued that the trial court has given cogent reasons for convicting the revisionist.
